comment: Written from the maker's source at commit 70a282a76d3a6da7fb84dd45aa1e4670538a951e, the commit that first carries version 2.0.4 in plugin.json. Two later commits also carry 2.0.4 and both add a second module, SDLines, and a redrawn SDOrcasHeartV2; the installed plugin.json lists only SDOrcasHeart, the installed res directory holds exactly the files res held at 70a282a (SDOrcasHeart.svg through SDOrcasHeart6.svg, sd_switch1_1_.svg, sd_scale_o2_1.svg — all moved to dev/shared_components in the later commits), and the installed build references res/SDOrcasHeart6.svg with no trace of SDLines or of its Horizontal/Vertical menu wording. So 70a282a is what shipped. EXP 1 and EXP 2 are configured as inputs, given jacks on the panel and never read anywhere in process(); the maker's own names for them say (unused), so both get a line saying nothing reads them. The module is monophonic throughout: every read is getVoltage() with no channel and every write is setVoltage() with no channel. The eight parameter CV inputs all go through one function, getValue(), which scales the jack by the parameter's span over 10V, adds the knob and clamps the total to the parameter's own range — so 10V always covers the whole of a knob's travel whatever the units, and a negative voltage subtracts until the total hits the knob's floor. The clock, reset and scale-switch jacks all use rescale(v, 0.1f, 2.f, 0.f, 1.f) into a default SchmittTrigger, which makes the rising threshold 2V and the falling threshold 0.1V. The two octave buttons are read through getValue() as well, so their jacks are level-sensed rather than edge-triggered: any voltage above 0V turns the octave on, and a negative voltage cancels a pressed button. The wiki says the CV inputs expect a 10V range quoted as -5V to +5V or 0V to +10V; the code takes any voltage and clamps the sum, so a bipolar cable works but only the part of it that moves the total inside the knob's range has any effect. The twelve scale switches of each scale share one line each, since they differ only in which note they switch in. The A and B lamps are lights rather than parameters and cannot be clicked for help.
